body: I just tried this PR on my hardware with GNOME/i3/sway/niri, and it seems to work for all of them. I can replicate that in a VM as well, except for niri, which seems to have some trouble starting in VMs for me, even without a greeter.
also works for me on gdm+niri.
Adding backport to this since I got bit by this bug on nixos-26.05
Tested this on hyprland, does not work, unfortunately.

> I'd also very much like to know why tf. GDM needs to leak its shit into my session at all

I don't think it needs to, or that it does this. Your session's `$PATH` shouldn't contain `${pkgs.gnome-session}/bin` with this PR. This makes sure the variables are present when `gdm` runs `gnome-shell` to show its login window; it shouldn't pass them down into your hyprland session. At least it doesn't for me in the GNOME session.
We are currently running gdm in an unsupported configuration (we should be using systemd-userdbd, but there are reasons we were unable to get it in for 26.05), so our workaround causes these issues AFAIK.

> .... and see if you get useful journalctl logs from it?

Logs [here](https://paste.jackr.eu/zmLAKBpoDve.syslog) :).  i've had bit of a hard time finding what exactly what logs are relevant, if i need to do something different please let me know!

I see gdm makes it to `start-hyprland` but I don't see a reason for it crashing (maybe the mentioned `debug:disable_logs = false` would add more context?)

I haven't tried hyprland locally yet, I'll let you know if I can reproduce it.
It's possible i've pasted the wrong logs... I dont get to hyprland at all. I can look more at this tomorrow!
